## Upstream changes 7.2.3 -> 7.3.0

**Verdict:** NEEDS ATTENTION — no breaking change forces a rebuild, but the email-processing behaviour change and the SSO/proxy header hardening both need a host-side check before or right after applying.

### Breaking changes
- Unprocessable inbound emails no longer become orphaned `FailedEmail` records; they now create a visible ticket titled "Unprocessable email" instead: *"Mail processing now creates a ticket for every email instead... No new `FailedEmail` records are created, so the health check and the system report no longer report new failures; records that exist before the update are kept and not migrated, and the rake tasks keep working on them."* (BREAKING_CHANGES.md, "Unprocessable emails no longer create `FailedEmail` records", filed under 7.2, already in effect at the version this host is leaving — see Data and dependencies below for why it is not counted against this upgrade). Confirmed as commit history in this range: "Fixes #6507 - Inbound emails that fail to parse are dropped instead of becoming tickets" plus its follow-up, so the behaviour is live as of 7.3.0 if not already live at 7.2.3.
- The SSO login now rejects conflicting login sources and the shipped nginx/Apache configs clear `Remote-User` in addition to `X-Forwarded-User`: *"The shipped `contrib/nginx/zammad.conf`... now also clear the `Remote-User` header next to `X-Forwarded-User`. The Docker images rebuild their nginx configuration from the shipped one on every start, so the change applies to them automatically."* This is filed under the 7.2 section of BREAKING_CHANGES.md and its commit ("Follow up 70f26207... Fixes #6481 - Users of single-sign-on-only systems must click through a login page that offers no choice") appears in this commit range, so treat it as applying with this upgrade if not already applied. Only relevant if SSO/`Remote-User` is in use.
- Inbound webhook JSON escaping and HMAC-SHA256 signature verification were fixed (`Fixes #6523`, `Fixes #6526`) — any receiver that worked around the previous broken escaping or missing signature support may need its workaround removed.

### Variables
- none found in the notes or in the compose/.env.example diff.

### Data and dependencies
- The notes describe no new companion-service version requirement for this range. The only version pin that moved is the application image itself (7.2.3 -> 7.3.0); Postgres, Redis, Elasticsearch, Memcached stay as already pinned in the compose file.
- Already true at 7.2.3 (not introduced by this upgrade): the `FailedEmail` removal and the SSO header hardening both carry a "7.2" heading in BREAKING_CHANGES.md, meaning the template's current deploy (7.2.3) already runs this behaviour. Re-confirm your nginx/Apache config (if hand-modified outside the Docker image) already clears `Remote-User`, and that any monitoring built on the old `FailedEmail` health-check metric has already been replaced by watching for "Unprocessable email" tickets.
